Mumbai PM2.5 Analysis (2023–2025)

Saket Choudhary and Darakhshan Nehal

Source: vignettes/delhi_choropleth_map.Rmd
delhi_choropleth_map.Rmd

Introduction

Methods

(GeoJSON boundary, NetCDF satellite data, CPCB comparison).

Dual line chart

CPCB data is ‘Real-time/Hourly’ while Satellite data is ‘Monthly/Annual Mean’. aggregated the ground data to monthly means to ensure a fair comparison.

The satellite data represents a spatial mean over the Mumbai GeoJSON area, whereas CPCB data is an average of point-source monitoring stations. Some divergence is expected due to this ‘point-to-area’ difference.

Choropleth Delhi

Prepare the data 

if (!require("pacman")) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}
#  Load packages
pacman::p_load(
  vayuayan,
  tidyverse,
  tidylog,
  terra,
  sf,
  tidyterra,
  gstat,
  ggview,
  gstat,
  sp,
  exactextractr
)
# Get Delhi Ground Data (CPCB)
delhi_ground <- cpcb_download_city_data(
  city = "Delhi",
  year = 2023,
  "delhi_aqi_2023.csv"
)

# Load the wide data
delhi_wide <- read.csv("delhi_aqi_2023.csv")

# Reshape from Wide to Long
delhi_ground <- delhi_wide %>%
  # Remove the 'Day' column and pivot all months
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Day,
    names_to = "Month_Name",
    values_to = "ground_pm25"
  ) %>%
  # Convert month names to numbers (January -> 1, etc.)
  mutate(month = match(Month_Name, month.name)) %>%
  # Remove any NAs (like Feb 30th) and aggregate to monthly mean
  filter(!is.na(ground_pm25)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(ground_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

print(delhi_ground)
# Extract the 12 months
delhi_sat_results <- lapply(1:12, function(m) {
  message(paste("Processing Month:", m))
  delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")
  stats <- pm25_get_stats(
    geojson_file = delhi_geojson,
    year = 2023,
    month = m
  )
  data.frame(month = m, sat_pm25 = stats$mean)
})

# Combine into satellite dataframe
delhi_sat_df <- do.call(rbind, delhi_sat_results)

# Check results
print(delhi_sat_df)
# Join the ground spikes with the new satellite spikes
delhi_final <- delhi_ground %>%
  inner_join(delhi_sat_df, by = "month")

Plotting line chart 

# Plotting the "Seasonal Reality"
ggplot(delhi_final, aes(x = month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)"),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(y = ground_pm25, color = "CPCB Ground"), size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = sat_pm25, color = "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)"), size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CPCB Ground" = "#d77027ff",
      "WUSTL Satellite (Monthly)" = "#4575b4"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Delhi 2023: PM2.5 Satellite data Vs CPCB Historical estimates",
    y = expression(paste("PM2.5 Concentration (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),
    x = NULL,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") #+
# ggview::canvas(width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)

For 2024 and 2025, the ground data is ready, but the satellite component is pending the official release of the NetCDF files from Washington University.

Geospatial analysis

Only satellite data

delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")
delhi_shape <- st_read(delhi_geojson)

# Load November Satellite file (202311)
# Make sure the name matches downloadeded .nc file
nov_file <- "pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.202311-202311.nc"
r_nov <- rast(nov_file)

# Crop and Mask the satellite data to Delhi's boundary
# This 'cuts' the global map into a Delhi-sized piece
delhi_raster <- crop(r_nov, vect(delhi_shape))
delhi_raster_masked <- mask(delhi_raster, vect(delhi_shape))

# Create Map
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = delhi_raster_masked) +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_shape,
    fill = NA,
    color = "royalblue4",
    linewidth = 0.65
  ) +
  scale_fill_whitebox_c(
    palette = "muted",
    name = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")"))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Spatial Distribution of PM2.5 in Delhi",
    subtitle = "Satellite Estimate: November 2023",
    caption = "Source: WUSTL ACAG V6.GL.02.04"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Station data 

# For the whole list of stations.
# Get ALL stations for Delhi
delhi_station_list <- cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi")
print(delhi_station_list)
# Add coordinates via OpenStreetMap geocoding
delhi_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(delhi_station_list)

# Save to avoid re-geocoding on every render
write.csv(
  delhi_station_list,
  "delhi_stations_with_coords.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

delhi_full_sf <- st_as_sf(
  delhi_station_list,
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = 4326
)

Choropleth (zonal statistics)

Objective: Correlation b/w sensors & pollution

delhi_geojson <- system.file("extdata", "delhi_ncr.geojson", package = "vayuayan")
delhi_districts <- st_read(delhi_geojson)

# Load the Satellite Raster (e.g., Nov 2023)
nov_raster <- rast("pm25_data/V6GL02.04.CNNPM25.GL.202311-202311.nc")

# Zonal Statistics: Get average PM2.5 per district
# Step to turn a heatmap into a choropleth
district_means <- terra::extract(
  nov_raster,
  vect(delhi_districts),
  fun = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Join the data back to the shapes
delhi_districts$sat_pm25 <- district_means[, 2]
ggplot() +
  # Choropleth layer
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_districts,
    aes(fill = sat_pm25),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  # Ground Stations (All 40)
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_full_sf,
    color = "royalblue4",
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.65
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "Spectral",
    direction = -1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Delhi District-Wise PM2.5 Choropleth",
    subtitle = "District colors = Satellite Average | Red dots = CPCB Station Locations",
    caption = "Do districts with more dots show better ground-satellite alignment?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggview::canvas(width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
